_meta.description: Full 30-question RAGAS evaluation, run on Kaggle GPU per kaggle/README.md, judge model qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0, embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Real production run (not the earlier n=2 local validation). Full per-question response/context text is not stored here (some rows are very large, one pathologically so - see anomalies below); scores are the complete real record. Regenerate via `python -m eval.ragas_eval` on Kaggle for full row-level text if needed.
known_issues: answer_relevancy is NaN for all 30 questions. Diagnosed (see LOG.md Phase 8 Kaggle entry): the underlying mechanism (RAGAS's synthetic reverse-question generation via structured JSON output against the judge LLM) works correctly in isolated local testing against the same qwen2.5:7b model - not a fundamental incompatibility. Most likely cause: concurrent-load-induced timeouts/malformed retries against a single Ollama instance during the full run, the same class of issue already found and partially mitigated via RunConfig tuning earlier in Phase 8. Not re-verified with a lower-concurrency run as of this report.

JPM-1's generated answer degenerated into a multi-thousand-character repetition loop (a known small/quantized-model failure mode - the model got stuck repeating one sentence). This corrupted faithfulness/context_precision scoring for that single row (both NaN); context_recall was unaffected since it doesn't depend on the generated response, only retrieved context vs. reference.

Custom '_id'/'_ticker' tracking columns added when building the RAGAS dataset were silently dropped by EvaluationDataset - per-question rows below are matched to test-set IDs by position (processing order matches data/eval/ragas_test_set.json's question order), not by an explicit ID RAGAS preserved.

mean_scores_note: answer_relevancy was NaN in the raw output (not JSON-serializable, reported as null) - see known_issues. Do not cite this metric until re-verified with a fix.

per_question.note: surprising - some claims in the response looked traceable to retrieved context on manual read; flagged as worth re-checking, see LOG.md
